reason: The text explicitly describes non-priests offering sacrifices to Yahweh. In Exodus 24:5, Moses 'sent young men of the people of Israel (נַעֲרֵי בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל) and they offered burnt offerings and sacrificed peace offerings to the Lord.' These were ordinary young men of the Israelite people, not designated priests. At this point in the narrative (at Mount Sinai, before the formal Aaronic priesthood is established in Leviticus 8), the text demonstrates that laypeople could perform sacrificial functions.
